summary: ​Mars Life is an interactive educational simulation game designed to teach players how to manage an autonomous space base and adaptive farm under extreme resource scarcity. Developed by students of Irkliiv Vocational Agrarian Lyceum, the project tackles both long-term deep-space exploration logistics and earthly agricultural crises (such as droughts and soil degradation) by modeling a closed-loop Bioregenerative Life Support System (BLSS). The simulator bridges vocational expertise—uniting tractor operators, mechanics, drivers, welders, and chefs—with cutting-edge space technology to demonstrate how local food, water, and oxygen production can sustain life beyond Earth.
details:
​What it does & How it works:
Mars Life is a fully interactive concept demonstrator where players manage 6 interconnected base modules (Habitat, Agrobiological Module, Recirculation, Power Grid, Command Center, and Engineering Bay). The system simulates continuous biological and physical loops:

​Air Loop: Crew exhales CO2 \rightarrow Plants absorb CO2 via photosynthesis \rightarrow Release O2.

​Water Loop: Wastewater and condensation are purified and 90% recycled back to hydroponics and the crew.

​Nutrient & Food Loop: Organic waste is mineralized into nutrient solutions for crops, feeding the crew with realistic energy constraints.
